title: Ted Bundy Escaped Custody Twice. Both Times, a Traffic Stop Caught Him
central_question: How did ordinary traffic stops keep catching Ted Bundy?
content_notes: Closed case: Bundy was convicted in Florida (1979, 1980) and executed on 24 Jan 1989. He appears ONLY as an anonymous rim-lit silhouette (tb28_bundy) or a dark head shape through a car's rear window, tagged 'ILLUSTRATION · NOT A LIKENESS': no face, no photo reference, never posed heroically or 'charming', none of his words quoted. The episode is about the police work, not his crimes: no victim is named or depicted, no violence, weapon or crime scene is shown; the items found in 1975 and the 1978 struggle are typed lines only. Officers are generic figures and are not named on screen. The cars are generic Beetle-shaped drawings with no badge and blank plates; courthouse, jail, gas station and streets are generic. No dramatisation, film or series is referenced. Every card is our own typed graphic. No dialogue is invented. Legal status verified 2026-10-12.

lines.text: Both times, a traffic stop caught him.
In Utah, a trooper chased his Volkswagen. No headlights.
Inside: a crowbar, a ski mask and handcuffs.
In Colorado, he jumped from a courthouse window.
Six days later, police stopped him in a stolen car.
Then he escaped through a jail ceiling.
The FBI put him on its Ten Most Wanted list.
In Pensacola, an officer checked a Volkswagen's plate.
It was stolen. The driver was Bundy.
Convicted in Florida, he was executed in 1989.

claims.text: Bundy escaped custody twice in Colorado in 1977: on 7 June 1977 he jumped from a second-floor law-library window of the Pitkin County Courthouse in Aspen during a hearing; on 30 December 1977 he escaped from the Garfield County Jail in Glenwood Springs through an opening in his cell ceiling (where a light fixture had been) into a crawl space.

Both escapes ended at a traffic stop in a stolen car: about six days after the Aspen escape, officers pulled over the stolen car he was driving (June 1977); after the jail escape, a Pensacola police officer stopped the stolen Volkswagen he was driving (15 February 1978). With the August 1975 Utah stop, traffic stops figured in three of his arrests.

Before his 1989 execution Bundy confessed to 30 murders (Britannica; other sources give 28 or 36); the true total is unknown. Spoken as 'He later confessed to 30 murders'; no victim is named or shown.

In the early hours of 16 August 1975, Utah Highway Patrol Sgt Bob Hayward saw a Volkswagen Beetle driving with its lights off in the Granger area of Salt Lake County; it fled and he pursued it until it pulled into a gas station. The trooper is not named on screen.

The Beetle's passenger seat had been removed; officers found items including a crowbar, a ski mask and handcuffs (also an ice pick, a pantyhose mask and garbage bags). Bundy was arrested - his first arrest - and was charged with possession of burglary tools days later. The items are named on a typed card only and never drawn.
The FBI added Bundy to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list on 10 February 1978 (fugitive no. 360); he was caught five days later.

On 15 February 1978, Pensacola police officer David Lee ran the licence plate of an orange Volkswagen Beetle; it came back stolen. He stopped the car and arrested the driver, Bundy, after a struggle. The officer is not named on screen; the struggle is a typed line, never shown.
Bundy was convicted in Florida in July 1979 (Miami trial) and February 1980 (Orlando trial) and sentenced to death; he was executed at Florida State Prison on 24 January 1989.
Memorial line: 'We remember his victims.' No victim is named or depicted; no number is given beyond the sourced confession figure.

The car of the 1975 stop was Bundy's tan 1968 Volkswagen Beetle (now displayed at the Alcatraz East Crime Museum); the 1978 car was a stolen orange Beetle. Our hero object is a generic Beetle-shaped car with no badge and a blank plate.
